summary: @ornikar/intl-config 10.0.4 ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: Version 10.0.4 of this scoped intl configuration package adds a `preinstall` script (`node setup.mjs`) that is not present in prior releases and not documented in the CHANGELOG (which stops at 10.0.1). `setup.mjs` is itself obfuscated (identifier mangling, string-array dispatcher) and, at `npm install` time, either invokes an existing `bun` on PATH or downloads the Bun 1.3.13 runtime from GitHub releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods the binary executable, and uses that freshly-downloaded alternate runtime to execute a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is 727 KB of heavily obfuscated JavaScript (rotated string-array dispatcher `WV8StW`, large opaque literal tables, `_0xXXXX` identifier mangling, `// @bun @bun-cjs` header) with no relationship to FormatJS/intl functionality. Prior versions of this package are pure intl configuration with no lifecycle hooks, no bundled runtime download, and no obfuscated payloads. The alternate-runtime + install-time execution + obfuscation + undocumented behavior + purpose mismatch pattern is the shape of a supply-chain hijack: arbitrary attacker code executes on every installer's machine via the auto-fired preinstall hook.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
